page_texts.4:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

A **value/behavioral invariant** — "for any valid input, property P holds" — cannot be proven by a finite set of examples, yet example-based (Gherkin/unit) tests are exactly finite. Without a verification technique that explores the input space, such invariants are asserted on the strength of a handful of hand-picked cases and their violations escape to production.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Specify the invariant as a **property-based test (PBT)**: define a generator that produces valid inputs across the space, assert the property over generated inputs, and enable **shrinking** so any counterexample is reduced to a minimal reproducer. This is the runtime/behavioral tier for the negative-property axis — the complement to architecture-fitness (which proves *structural* invariants statically).
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- An invariant registered as `tier: property` (per STD-GOV-QA-002) — a value or round-trip property over a large/continuous input space.
- Examples: "adjudicated amount is never negative"; "`decode(encode(m)) == m`"; "a sort's output is always a permutation of its input"; "no computation overflows for any valid input".
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Explores the input space instead of a few hand-picked cases — finds edge cases authors miss.
- Shrinking yields a minimal failing input, making defects fast to diagnose.
- Gives the `property` test type (STD-APP-TEST-001) a concrete authoring technique.
page_texts.9:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

In a claims/enrollment platform, value-correctness invariants ("a member is never charged a negative amount", "eligibility dates never invert") are correctness- and compliance-critical. An example test proves one case; a business needs assurance across the whole range of real inputs.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The negative-property axis has two verification tiers: **architecture-fitness** (structural, static — PTN-APP-GOV-001) and **property-based** (behavioral, runtime — this pattern). The pipeline declares a `property` test type, but without an authoring technique, teams either skip it or fake it with a couple of example assertions.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Consider "for any valid `Claim`, member-owed ≥ 0". A developer writes three example claims that all pass; a fourth shape (a full-refund with a coordination-of-benefits adjustment) would produce −$5, but no one enumerated it. The example suite is green; the invariant is false.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- **Coverage vs cost** — generating and shrinking inputs costs more than a fixed example, but covers vastly more.
- **Generator fidelity** — a generator that produces only "easy" inputs proves little; it must cover boundaries and adversarial shapes.
- **Determinism in CI** — PBT uses randomness; runs must be reproducible (seeded) so failures are actionable.
page_texts.14:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

For each `property`-tier invariant: (1) write a **generator** for the input type covering the valid space including boundaries; (2) express the **property** as an assertion that must hold for every generated input; (3) enable **shrinking** so a failure reduces to a minimal counterexample; (4) run it in CI with a fixed seed (and a regression corpus of past counterexamples) so it is deterministic and gates the build.
page_texts.15:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
   generator ──► many valid inputs ──► property assertion
                        (boundaries,        │
                         adversarial)        ├─ holds for all sampled ─► PASS
                                             └─ fails for one ─► shrink ─► minimal counterexample ─► FAIL(build)
                                                                                     │
                                                                              add to regression corpus
```
page_texts.16:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Generator | produce valid inputs across the space (incl. boundaries) | the input type/model |
| Property assertion | the "for all" invariant to hold | the registered `INV-*` |
| Shrinker | reduce a failing input to a minimal reproducer | PBT framework |
| CI harness | run seeded, gate the build, keep a regression corpus | `TEST-HARNESS-property` (STD-APP-TEST-001) |
page_texts.17:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

The invariant is registered (`INV-*`, STD-GOV-QA-002) and routed to the `property` tier. This pattern implements it as a PBT in the `TEST-HARNESS-property` harness, invoked in CI. A discovered counterexample fails the build, is shrunk, and is added to the regression corpus so it is permanently guarded.
page_texts.18:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Round-trip / metamorphic** — `decode(encode(x)) == x`; `parse(render(x)) == x`.
- **Invariant preservation** — an operation preserves a data invariant for all inputs (balances sum to zero, sets stay unique).
- **Model-based** — the system-under-test matches a simplified reference model over a generated sequence of operations.
page_texts.20:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- The invariant registered as `tier: property` (STD-GOV-QA-002).
- An operational `TEST-HARNESS-property` (STD-APP-TEST-001) with a PBT framework (Hypothesis / fast-check / proptest).
page_texts.22:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#phase-1-model-the-input]

#### Phase 1: Model the input

1. Define a generator for the input type covering the valid range, boundaries, and adversarial shapes.
2. Constrain the generator to *valid* inputs (or filter), so failures are real property violations, not invalid-input noise.
page_texts.23:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#phase-2-assert-shrink-gate]

#### Phase 2: Assert, shrink, gate

1. Express the property as an assertion over a generated input.
2. Enable shrinking; run seeded in CI so failures reproduce.
3. On a counterexample: fix the defect, add the shrunk case to a regression corpus.
page_texts.25:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#example-hypothesis--python]

#### Example (Hypothesis / Python)

```python
from hypothesis import given, settings, strategies as st

# INV-CLAIMS-002: for any valid Claim, member-owed >= 0
@settings(deadline=None, derandomize=True)  # deterministic in CI
@given(claim=valid_claims())                # generator over the valid space
def test_member_owed_never_negative(claim):
    result = adjudicate(claim)
    assert result.member_owed >= 0          # the "for all" property
```
page_texts.27:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Invest in the generator — coverage of boundaries and adversarial shapes is where PBT earns its value.
- Seed runs (derandomize) so CI failures are reproducible; keep a regression corpus of past counterexamples.
- One property per test, tied to one registered `INV-*`, so a failure maps to a specific invariant.
page_texts.28:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Weak generator** — only "easy" inputs; the property looks proven but the space is unexplored.
- **Non-deterministic CI** — unseeded runs produce flaky, un-actionable failures.
- **Property that restates the implementation** — asserting what the code does rather than an independent invariant proves nothing.

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** `INV-CLAIMS-002` — member-owed never negative.
**Implementation:** a Hypothesis property with a `valid_claims()` generator; shrinking reduced a failure to a minimal refund-with-COB case.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-007-property-based-test-specification-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** A value/behavioral "for all" invariant can't be proven by finite example tests, so its violations escape.

**Solution:** Specify it as a property-based test — a generator over the input space, a property assertion, and shrinking to a minimal counterexample — run seeded in CI.

**When to Use:** Any invariant registered as `tier: property` (value/round-trip/metamorphic properties over a large input space).

**Key Benefits:**
- Explores the input space, finding edge cases authors miss
- Shrinking gives a minimal, actionable reproducer
- Gives the `property` test type a concrete authoring technique

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** The invariant registered (`tier: property`); an operational `TEST-HARNESS-property` with a PBT framework.

**Related Patterns:** PTN-APP-GOV-001 (fitness — structural sibling), PTN-APP-GOV-003 (runtime monitor).
